source_text: Ἕως γὰρ μόνος ἦν ὁ ἄνθρωπος, οὐκ εἶχε λαβὴν ὁ διάβολος, ἐπεὶ δὲ ἐκτίσθη ἡ γυνὴ, ἁπαλὸν ζῶον, ἀναγκαίως τοῦ Δημιουργοῦ τὴν ἁπαλότητα φυσικὴν ἐμποιήσαντος, ἵνα ὑπὸ τοῦ φιλανθρώπου εὐμαρῶς τραφῇ τὰ νήπια. Εἰ γὰρ αὐστηρὰ ἦν ἡ γυνὴ, οὐκ ἂν ἀποκλαιόμενον τὸ νήπιον τοῖς στήθεσιν ἐνηγκαλίζετο· οὐκ ἂν τῆς ἰδίας τροφῆς ἠμέλει, τὸν δὲ μαζὸν ἐπεῖχε πρὸς ὠφέλειαν τοῦ ὑπομαζίου παιδίου. Νῦν μέντοι μητέρων εὐσπλαγχνίαι τὸν ὕπνον πολλάκις τῶν βλεφάρων ἀποδιώκουσιν, ἐπειδὰν μικρὸν παρενοχληθῇ τὸ νήπιον. Ἵνα τοίνυν ἐκτρέφηται νήπιον, ἁπαλὴ ἡ φύσις ἡ γυναικεία παρήχθη, ἁπαλὴ καὶ φιλάνθρωπος. Τῷ οὖν ἁπαλῷ καὶ τῷ εἰκτικῷ προσχὼν ὁ διάβολος, τὴν εὐκολίαν τὴν πρὸς ἀρετὴν, εὐκολίαν εἰς κακίαν ἐποιήσατο. Τοῦτο οὖν ἐστιν ἴδιον τὸ κακὸν τοῦ διαβόλου, ὁ φθόνος· φθόνος ὁ ἐκλαληθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενος, ὁ ἰατρείαν οὐκ ἐπιδεχόμενος. Ὁ κεφαλὴν ἀλγῶν λέγει τῷ ἰατρῷ τὴν κεφαλαλγίαν· ὁ φθόνον νοσῶν τί εἴπῃ; Λυπεῖ με τὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ ἀγαθά; Ἡ μὲν ἀλήθεια αὕτη· τὰ δὲ ῥήματα ἕκαστος ἐπαισχύνεται. Τί στενάζεις; ἴδιον κακὸν, ἢ ἀλλότριον ἀγαθόν; Τοὺς μὲν γὰρ κύνας τρέφοντες ἡμεροῦμεν· τὸν δὲ βάσκανον εὐεργετοῦντες χαλεπώτερον ἀπεργαζόμεθα. Οὐ γὰρ χαίρει ἐφ' οἷς ἂν πάθῃ χρηστοῖς· ἀλλὰ λυπεῖται τῇ σῇ εὐπορίᾳ, ὅτι ἔχεις ὕλην, ὅθεν τὴν χρείαν αὐτῷ πληρώσεις. Μὴ τοίνυν συνεμπέσῃς εἰς τὴν ἀπάτην τοῦ διαβόλου· ἐβάσκηνέ σοι, ἐβάσκηνεν· ἐξώρισέ σε τοῦ παραδείσου. Δι' ἐκεῖνον ἄκανθαι, δι' ἐκεῖνον ἱδρὼς, δι' ἐκεῖνον ὁ τόπος τῆς ἐξορίας· εἰς ὃν ἐκπεσὼν, μὴ ἐπιλάθῃ τῆς πατρίδος τῆς ἀρχαίας. Μέμνησο τῆς εὐγενείας τῆς σεαυτοῦ· μέμνησο τῆς πατρίδος ὅθεν ἐξωρίσθης. Μέμνησο τοῦ τὰ τηλικαῦτά σε ζημιώσαντος· μὴ σπείσῃ πρὸς αὐτὸν, μηδέ ποτε τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁμιλίαν καταδέξῃ. Δύο γὰρ ἠδίκησε, καὶ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἐξέβαλε, καὶ νῦν τὴν ἐπάνοδον διακόπτει Ἐβάσκηνέ σοι τῶν πρώτων ἀγαθῶν διὰ γυναικὸς, καὶ πάλιν ἐπινοίαις ταῖς κατὰ τὴν γυναῖκα εἰς τὴν ἀποκατάστασιν κωλύει. Πορνείαν ἐπενόησεν, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθῃς εἰς παράδεισον. Οὐκ ἤρκεσεν αὐτῷ ἡ πρώτη ζημία, ὅτι κατέστρεψεν· ἀλλὰ δευτέρας μεθοδείας ἐπινοεῖ, τὸν δρόμον ἡμῖν ἐπέχων. Κλέπτει διὰ τοῦ ψεύδους, ἐπειδὴ τεῖχός ἐστι τοῖς ὁδεύουσιν εἰς παράδεισον τὸ ψεῦδος. Τὰ ἐκείνου ἐπιτηδεύματα μυρία. Τὰ ἐκείνου βλαστήματα, ὠμότης, τραχύτης, πλεονεξία, λοιδορία· πάντα ὅσα μισεῖ ὁ λόγος τῆς ἀληθείας, ταῦτα τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστί. Μισάνθρωπος, ἐπειδὴ καὶ θεομάχος. Ἐμίσησε πρότερον, ἐτραχηλίασε κατὰ Θεοῦ παντοκράτορος, κατεφρόνησε τοῦ Δεσπότου, ἠλλοτριώθη τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἐπειδὴ εἶδε τὸν ἄνθρωπον κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν Θεοῦ, μὴ δυνάμενος εἰς Θεὸν τραπῆναι, εἰς τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ πονηρίαν ἐκένωσεν· ὥσπερ εἴ τις ἄνθρωπος ὀργισθεὶς τὴν εἰκόνα λιθάζοι, ἐπειδὴ τὸν βασιλέα οὐ δύναται, τὸ ξύλον τύπτων, τὸ τὴν μίμησιν ἔχον. Εἶδον ἐγὼ τὰ μισανθρωπότατα τῶν ζώων ἐν τοῖς σταδίοις πολλάκις, ἢ εἶδον, ἢ ἤκουσα· ἀσφαλὴς γὰρ ἔστω ὁ λόγος. Πλὴν ὅτι αὐταὶ αἱ παρδάλεις φυσικήν τινα ἔχουσι πρὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον ὀργὴν, καὶ πεφύκασι μάλιστα τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐφάλλεσθαι. Οἱ τοίνυν καταπαίζοντες τῆς μανίας τοῦ θηρίου ἐν χάρτῃ εἰκόνα προδεικνύουσιν ὡς ἄνθρωπον.
thought_title: The devil envies man and attacks Gods image in man
orientation: The preacher is showing how envy is the devils own evil and how the devil turned mans softness toward virtue into softness toward vice.
pass_a_gloss: For as long as man was alone, the devil had no hold. But when woman was created, a tender living creature, since the Creator of necessity made tenderness natural, so that infants might be easily nourished by the loving to mankind one. For if woman were harsh, she would not have embraced in her breasts the infant crying aloud. She would not have neglected her own food, but she held out the breast for the benefit of the little child under the breast. But as things are, compassions of mothers often drive sleep away from their eyelids, whenever the infant is troubled a little. So then, in order that an infant may be reared, the female nature was brought forth tender, tender and loving to mankind. The devil therefore, applying himself to what is tender and to what is yielding, made the readiness toward virtue a readiness toward vice. This therefore is the devils own evil, envy. Envy that cannot be spoken out, that admits no healing. One aching in the head tells the physician his headache. One sick with envy, what will he say. Do the goods of my brother grieve me. This is the truth, but each one is ashamed of the words. Why do you groan. At your own evil, or at another mans good. For by feeding dogs we tame them, but by benefiting the envious man we render him harsher. For he does not rejoice at whatever kind things he may suffer, but he is grieved at your prosperity, because you have material from which you will fulfill his need. Do not then fall together into the deception of the devil. He envied you, he envied. He drove you in exile from paradise. Because of him thorns, because of him sweat, because of him the place of exile, into which having fallen out, do not forget the ancient homeland. Remember your own nobility. Remember the homeland from which you were driven in exile. Remember the one who damaged you in such great things. Make no treaty with him, nor ever accept company with him. For he did wrong in two ways, both he cast out from the beginning, and now he cuts off the return. He envied you for the first goods through woman, and again by devices against woman he hinders you toward restoration. He devised sexual immorality, in order that you may not enter into paradise. The first damage did not suffice for him, that he overthrew, but he devises a second scheme, holding back the course for us. He steals through falsehood, since falsehood is a wall for those journeying into paradise. His pursuits are countless. His offshoots are cruelty, harshness, greed, abuse. All as many things as the word of truth hates, these are of the devil. Hater of mankind, since also fighter against God. He hated beforehand, he stiffened the neck against almighty God, he despised the Master, he was estranged from God. Since he saw man according to image and likeness of God, being unable to turn against God, he emptied his own wickedness into the image of God, just as if some man in anger were to stone the image, since he cannot stone the king, beating the wood, that which has the imitation. I have seen the most hating of mankind among living creatures in the stadiums often, or I saw, or I heard, for let the account be safe. Except that the leopards themselves have a certain natural anger toward man, and they are by nature to leap especially at the eyes of men. Those therefore mocking the madness of the wild beast show beforehand in paper an image as a man.

pass_b_english: While man stood alone, the devil found no hold for attack. Then woman was created, a tender creature. The Creator made tenderness part of her nature, so infants would feed easily under her loving care. If woman had been harsh, she would never have clasped a crying infant to her breast. She would never have neglected her own food and held out her breast for the good of the child beneath it. Even now a mother's compassion often drives sleep from her eyelids when her infant is only slightly troubled. A child needs such nursing, so woman's nature came forth tender, tender and loving.

The devil fastened on what was tender and yielding. He turned a readiness meant for virtue into a readiness for evil. This is the devil's own evil. It is envy, envy that cannot be spoken aloud, envy that admits no cure. A man with a aching head tells the doctor about his headache. What can a man sick with envy say? Can he say, “My brother's goods grieve me?” That would be the truth, but everyone feels shame to speak those words. Why are you groaning? Is it for your own evil or for another's good? We tame dogs by feeding them. We make the envious man harsher by doing him good. He takes no joy in the kindness he receives. He grieves at your prosperity, because you have the means to meet his need.

So do not fall into the devil's deceit. He envied you. He envied you. He drove you out of paradise. Because of him come thorns (Genesis 3:18). Because of him comes sweat (Genesis 3:19). Because of him comes this place of exile. You have fallen into it, so do not forget your ancient homeland. Remember your own nobility. Remember the homeland from which you were exiled. Remember the one who damaged you so greatly. Make no treaty with him. Never accept his company. He has wronged you twice. He cast you out in the beginning, and now he blocks your return. He envied you for your first blessings through woman, and again he hinders your restoration by schemes involving woman. He invented sexual sin to keep you from entering paradise. The first damage did not satisfy him, when he overthrew you. He invents a second plot and blocks our course. He steals through falsehood, for falsehood stands like a wall across the path of those journeying to paradise. His practices are countless. His offshoots are cruelty, harshness, greed, and abuse. All that the word of truth hates belongs to the devil.

He hates humanity because he fights against God. He hated first. He stiffened his neck against God Almighty. He despised the Master. He estranged himself from God. Then he saw man made in the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26). He could not turn against God, so he emptied his wickedness upon God's image. He acts like an angry man who stones the emperor's portrait because he cannot reach the emperor, striking the wood that bears the likeness. I have often watched the most man-hating beasts in the arenas. Or rather, whether I saw them or heard of them, let my account stand as sure. Leopards hold a natural rage against man, and by nature they spring above all at the eyes of men. So the men who mock the beast's frenzy hold up a likeness of a man drawn on paper.
